news.headline: Tenax CEO Tells Cantor Healthcare Conference LEVEL Miss Was a Patient-Selection Problem, Not a Drug-Failure Verdict
news.summary: President and CEO Chris Giordano used the 12th Annual Cantor Fitzgerald Global Healthcare Conference to reframe the LEVEL trial's walk-distance miss as a lesson in enrolling too broad a population, pointing again to the strong biomarker, hemodynamic and enriched-subgroup signals as the basis for the planned FDA/EMA discussions. It was management's first scheduled public forum since the full dataset was unveiled at ESC on August 29.

news.headline: ADAR1 Capital/Daniel Schneeberger Stake in Tenax Therapeutics Climbs to Roughly 14-15% After Week-Long Buying Streak
news.summary: Funds tied to ADAR1 Capital Management and 10%-plus owner Daniel Schneeberger, already holding a reported 12.97% stake (4.85 million shares) as of August 24, kept buying through early September at roughly $1.78-$1.80 a share, pushing their combined position to around 14-15% of shares outstanding. It remains the clearest bullish signal in the stock since the LEVEL primary-endpoint miss.

news.headline: Wall Street Settles on Consensus Hold Rating for Tenax Therapeutics After Post-LEVEL Analyst Shakeout
news.summary: Aggregating the ten brokerages that cover the stock, MarketBeat reported an average Hold rating (1 Strong Buy, 3 Buy, 5 Hold, 1 Sell) and a consensus price target near $14, a figure still skewed by pre-LEVEL-miss targets that had not all been refreshed. The mixed spread underscores how unsettled sell-side opinion remains nearly a month after the trial's primary-endpoint failure.

news.headline: Guggenheim Cuts Tenax Therapeutics to Neutral as Analysts Split Over Enriched-Subgroup Rescue Strategy
news.summary: Guggenheim moved off its already-reduced Buy rating (cut to a $4 target right after the August 10 miss) to Neutral with no price target, citing continued clinical and regulatory uncertainty after digesting the full ESC dataset, while Piper Sandler and Canaccord Genuity kept Buy ratings with $4 targets on the strength of the enriched-subgroup data. The split highlights how differently analysts are weighing the sub-333m-walk-distance subgroup benefit against the overall trial failure.

news.headline: Tenax Presents Full Phase 3 LEVEL Dataset as Late-Breaker at ESC Congress 2026 in Munich
news.summary: Professor Sanjiv Shah presented the complete LEVEL dataset: in the prespecified subgroup with baseline 6-minute walk distance below the trial median of 333m, levosimendan improved 6MWD by 26.3m versus placebo (p=0.0112), cut NT-proBNP by roughly 47-49%, and improved right ventricular systolic pressure and roughly 20 echocardiographic parameters across every domain measured. This subgroup and biomarker depth underpins Tenax's plan to pursue a narrower, enriched registrational path with the FDA and EMA.

news.headline: Tenax Therapeutics Announces Topline Results from Phase 3 LEVEL Clinical Trial of TNX-103 in Patients with PH-HFpEF
news.summary: The pivotal LEVEL trial missed its primary endpoint (6-minute walk distance, +3.5m vs placebo, p=0.63) and its key secondary endpoint (KCCQ), though prespecified subgroups of sicker patients showed a meaningful walk-distance benefit and strong biomarker/hemodynamic effects. Shares collapsed roughly 87-90% on the news, and Tenax said it would seek an FDA Type C meeting (and EMA scientific consultation) to discuss a revised registrational path using an enrichment strategy.

catalysts.label: FDA Type C meeting on levosimendan path forward
catalysts.detail: Tenax plans to request a Type C meeting with the FDA (and a parallel EMA scientific consultation) to discuss an enrichment strategy for a revised registrational program, leaning on the subgroup and biomarker data presented at ESC and the FDA's earlier agreement that a single well-controlled Phase 3 with p=0.01 could support an NDA. The outcome will determine whether LEVEL-2 is modified or a new study is required; no meeting date has been publicly confirmed yet.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings and cash-runway/strategy update
catalysts.detail: The next quarterly report should update the cash position (guided to a runway through Q2 2028 as of June 30, 2026, with $118.0 million in cash plus $8.1 million of post-quarter warrant exercises) along with concrete next steps for the levosimendan program following the LEVEL miss, including any outcome from the planned FDA Type C meeting. Exact date not yet announced; Tenax reported Q2 results on July 31, 2026.

catalysts.label: LEVEL-2 Phase 3 enrollment completion
catalysts.detail: The global, roughly 540-patient LEVEL-2 registrational trial (2:1 randomization, over 100 sites across 15 countries) remains ongoing, with enrollment completion guided to end of 2027. Design and eligibility criteria may still be revised pending FDA feedback from the planned Type C meeting, potentially shifting toward the enriched, lower-baseline-walk-distance population highlighted at ESC.

pulse: TENX has stabilized around $2.00-2.20, well off its post-LEVEL-miss lows, as insider buying by ADAR1 Capital/Daniel Schneeberger (now roughly 14-15% of shares outstanding) offsets a split and still-cautious sell-side, with Guggenheim cutting to Neutral on August 31 even as Piper Sandler and Canaccord kept $4 Buy ratings on the strength of the enriched-subgroup data shown at ESC (a ~26m walk-distance benefit and ~47-49% NT-proBNP reduction in patients below the 333m baseline median). Management used the September 9 Cantor Global Healthcare Conference to reinforce its narrative that LEVEL was a patient-selection problem rather than a drug-failure verdict, ahead of a still-unscheduled FDA Type C meeting (with parallel EMA consultation) that will decide whether a narrower, enriched LEVEL-2 registrational path is viable. With cash guided into Q2 2028, the company has runway to await that regulatory feedback without an imminent financing need.
